title: The Globe
desc: A terrestrial globe on a brass stand. Every library kept one long before anyone could look a place up in a second: it is the original way to see where a story is set. The places in the books on these shelves are all on it somewhere.

title: The Reference Desk
where: The Reading Room, by the hall
desc: Where you ask. Librarians were the first search engine: this is the desk where a question gets answered, a book gets found and a visitor gets pointed the right way. Nobody has ever been turned away from one for not knowing what they were looking for.

title: The North Reading Table
desc: A long oak table under three green-shaded banker's lamps. The lamps throw their light down on to the page and keep it out of your eyes, which is why reading rooms have used them for over a century. Sit anywhere: the chairs are leather and the table is meant to be leaned on.

title: The South Reading Table
desc: The second of the room's two reading tables, a mirror of the first across the hall. Rooms like this were built so that anyone could walk in off the street and sit down with a book for nothing, which is the oldest promise a public library makes.

title: The Grand Piano
desc: A grand piano with its lid propped open, turned so the keyboard faces the room. Libraries have always been about more than books: lectures, readings, recitals. The lid is up because a grand is meant to be heard across a room this size, and the bench is out because someone was just playing.

title: The Spiral Stair
desc: Nineteen treads winding round a brass newel, up to the gallery that runs right round the room. The upper shelves are up there. Go on up: the handrail climbs with you, and the gallery is wide enough to walk the whole way round and look down on the hall.

title: The Arched Window
desc: The room's one great window, set in the west wall so the afternoon sun comes straight down the hall. Reading rooms were laid out this way before electric light: the tables sit where the daylight falls. Beyond the glass are the hills.

title: The Gallery
where: The Reading Room, up the spiral stair
desc: You made it up. The gallery runs round all four walls behind a panelled parapet, with the upper shelves at your shoulder and the whole hall laid out below: the checkered floor, the runner, the chandeliers at eye level. The quietest seat in the building is the one you are standing in.
